entities.name: William Sharpe
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
William Sharpe (1742–1818) was an American patriot politician from North Carolina who served in the Continental Congress (1779–1782) during the most critical years of the Revolutionary War in the South. North Carolina's role in the southern theater was crucial — the state was the site of major battles including Guilford Court House (1781), where Nathanael Greene's army wore down Cornwallis's forces before the British general's fateful march to Virginia and Yorktown. Sharpe served in Congress during the darkest southern period — after the fall of Charleston and Camden — through to the final victory.

He was a Rowan County North Carolina lawyer who represented the Piedmont Presbyterian Scots-Irish community that formed North Carolina's backbone of Revolutionary resistance.

The Continental Congress years were the republic's most desperate — the challenge of financing and supplying Washington's army while managing the British southern campaign.

He contributed to North Carolina's Revolutionary political legacy.
